motion.$description: RATIFIED (2026-07-25) from a real-usage audit of all 5 apps' CSS/Vue transitions — no app uses an animation library (no GSAP, Framer Motion, Lenis, or @vueuse/motion anywhere). client-web's single `animejs` usage (one chat-bubble fade-in) is real but a single-feature dependency, not load-bearing enough to design tokens around. career-web has a hand-rolled IntersectionObserver scroll-reveal used only on its one marketing landing page (Home.vue) — the one legitimately choreography-heavy surface in the suite, and even that is plain CSS underneath, not a library. ⚠️ CRITICAL, from the same audit: `prefers-reduced-motion` is handled in only 1 of 5 apps (career-web, 11 files) — client-web, client-dashboard, recruitment-portal, and dashboard have zero handling. This is a real, current accessibility gap, the motion equivalent of the contrast findings elsewhere in this file, not a token to define but a gap every app should close.

duration.$description: Confirmed by real usage: every one of the 5 apps independently clusters around the same handful of values despite no shared code or library between them — 150ms, 250ms, and 500ms each show up as a top-3 value in all 5 codebases. 200ms/300ms appear too as secondary values (overlapping with Tailwind's own stock transitionDuration scale), but 150/250/500 are the tightest, most-evidenced cluster and are kept as the named scale rather than the full Tailwind stock set, to stay small and intentional.

fast.$description: Micro-interactions: hover/focus color or shadow changes, button state changes. The single most common value in client-web (61 uses) and recruitment-portal (51 uses).

base.$description: The default for most transitions — dashboard's single most common value (85 uses) and client-dashboard's (28 uses). Use this when in doubt.

slow.$description: Larger surface changes: modal/drawer open-close, page-level transitions. career-web's single most common value (14 uses), also present at real volume in every other app (17-23 uses each).

easing.$description: Only two values matter anywhere in the real data: plain `ease` and `ease-in-out` are the top two curves in every single app, and nothing else is competitive except `linear` for spinners/marquees (a distinct, legitimate second case, not a general-purpose easing). The 5 apps split roughly 3-to-2 on which of `ease`/`ease-in-out` is their own top pick, so no amount of evidence alone resolves which becomes canonical — `standard` was set to `ease-in-out` by explicit decision (2026-07-25), not by vote count, as the more deliberate, named choice; recruitment-portal's margin in its favor (127 vs 53) was also the widest of any app either direction.

standard.$description: Canonical general-purpose easing, chosen 2026-07-25. Use for the vast majority of transitions (color, shadow, transform, opacity).

linear.$description: Reserved for continuous/looping motion only — spinners, marquees, indeterminate progress. Confirmed as the real, consistent choice for these specific cases across all 5 apps; never used as a general transition easing anywhere in the real data.
